newsitem.title: USA: Two Freemen passed $425,000 in bad checks in N.C..
newsitem.headline: Two Freemen passed $425,000 in bad checks in N.C..

text.p: A federal jury convicted two followers of the Freemen anti-government group Friday of bank fraud to buy vehicles for the Montana-based organisation.
The jury found Russell Landers and James Wells guilty of cashing $425,000 in bad checks at a Durham, N.C. bank.

Wells, 58, convicted of 12 counts, faces a maximum of 104 years in prison and $4.3 million in fines. Landers, 45, guilty on seven counts, faces as much as 31 years behind bars and $1.5 million in fines.
Sentencing was not expected for several weeks. They will remain in a North Carolina prison prior to sentencing.
The two bought a Chevrolet Suburban and a motor home with the money and then drove the vehicles from North Carolina to Montana last winter, the court was told.
According to court records the men were going to use the vehicles in a plot by the Freemen to kidnap, try and execute public officials in Montana.
However, the FBI attempted to arrest the Freemen, triggering an 81-day armed standoff on a ranch near Jordan in Montana.
